title: A Finite Element Analysis of Stackable Surgical Guide System for Flapless Dental Implants Insertion in Fully Edentulous Maxilla
content: Stackable surgical templates enable flapless, prosthetically driven implant placement and immediate provizionalization in complete-arch rehabilitation, yet intraoperative guide fracture remains a recognized complication, and the biomechanics of the complete multi-component assembly on the edentulous maxilla have not been characterized. This in silico study used 3D modeling, surface refinement and finite element analysis (CATIA v5) to evaluate the stress and displacement distribution within a four-component model—maxilla, polymeric base guide, implant-supported guide, and grade-4 titanium 5 fixation pins—derived from a prosthetically driven virtual plan. Materials were modeled as homogeneous, isotropic, and linearly elastic, and a maximum simulated axial drilling force of 10.14 N with an associated friction-derived torsional moment was applied for a Ø2 mm osteotomy, under both idealized bonded and frictional contact conditions. The maximum von Mises stresses were 2.34 MPa (maxilla), 3.18 MPa (base guide), and 4.32 MPa (implant guide), with pins below 3.26 MPa—all well beneath the admissible strength of each material. The implant-supported guide was the most stressed component (~7.2% utilization), whereas the titanium pins operated below 1%, and the maximum deformation was 0.074 mm. Within its limitations, the study shows that the polymeric guides, not the metallic pins, govern the mechanical safety margin of stackable guide systems.
